environment.storage: local NVMe for every input, output and scratch file

method: STAR Suite 1.9.4 integrated trimming, alignment and TranscriptVB quantification (with and without in-process Y-chromosome removal) on the PPARG revertant WT replicate 3 paired-end library (35,089,336 read pairs) was compared with an external stepwise pipeline on the same input: Trim Galore 0.6.10 with FastQC, upstream STAR 2.7.11b with TranscriptomeSAM output, an awk/samtools/gzip Y split when Y removal is on, and Salmon 1.10.3 in alignment mode with automatic library-type detection (-l A, which detects the stranded ISR layout) and GC-bias correction. Runs were made one at a time on a quiet machine with the page cache dropped first; elapsed time is whole-process wall-clock time from /usr/bin/time. Quantification parity compares estimated read counts (NumReads) against Salmon on the no-Y-removal benchmark, at gene and transcript level, by Spearman and Pearson correlation over all features.
limitations: Each timing is one completed run rather than a replicated distribution.
The superseded record used an earlier 1.7.0 candidate and a different external wrapper; its 1.81-fold figure is not comparable with this comparison.

An earlier recording of this external control ran Salmon with -l IU, which is unstranded and assigns antisense reads to opposite-strand genes on this stranded library; the values here come from the re-recorded control with -l A.
Wall-clock values depend on hardware, storage, cache state and tool versions.
